rationale: Test the registered full multimodal pointcloud reward with conservative guidance and a constant ramp. Its attraction targets originate in stage-specific historical elite coordinates; mixture weights require historical affinity scores. These targets are geometrical hypotheses, not binding energies. Positive short-scale pair kernels and reduced local y spread motivate testing coordinate guidance, but do not establish that elite matching improves pIC50 or that this family wins. The 0.1 guidance ratio limits intervention strength; ramp power 0 avoids inferring a spatial force or schedule from temporal deltas. Use the registered FLOWR endpoint VJP with correspondence detached. Keep the supplied execution window and assess final predicted target pIC50 and secondary strain.
failure_modes: Selected endpoint associations cannot establish causal benefit; no candidate-family outcome comparison supports a winner.
Historical elite coordinates and affinity weights may encode selection bias or transfer poorly to new graph states.
Pointcloud attraction may compress geometry, increase strain, or create receptor clashes despite improving geometric similarity.
Differentiating correspondence, substituting time derivatives for spatial gradients, or bypassing the FLOWR endpoint VJP invalidates the intended force.
Whole-scalar reward rescaling may cancel under gradient normalization; component weights instead change direction.
No affinity-head gradient or particle selection is available; weak adjusted survival evidence does not support claims about either mechanism.
